points.quote: `workbench.desktop.main.ts` imports `workbench.common.main.js` (line 15). It then adds the Electron pieces
`workbench.web.main.ts` also imports `workbench.common.main.js` (line 16). It then adds `./browser/web.main.js` and browser-only services

`src/vs/workbench/workbench.common.main.ts` holds everything shared. ... `workbench.desktop.main.ts` imports `workbench.common.main.js` ... `workbench.web.main.ts` also imports `workbench.common.main.js`
**Platform-specific implementations sit behind a shared interface.** Each platform registers its own implementation of the same service interface
The two builds share code through three entry-point files, and a feature's code is loaded only if one of them imports it.
If no entry point imports a `*.contribution.ts` file, it is never bundled or run.
